chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad al-Bandaneeji narrated from Ubaydillah ibn Musa al-Alawi, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn al-Mustaneer, from Abdurrahman ibn al-Qassim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Abbas, who said:

The Messenger of God said to my father: 'O Abbas, woe to my progeny from your progeny, and woe to your progeny from my progeny.' He said: 'O Messenger of God, should I avoid women?' (Or he said: 'Should I restrain myself?') He said: 'Indeed, God's knowledge has passed (been determined) and the affairs are in His hand, and indeed the command will be in my progeny.'
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the relationship between his progeny and Abbas's progeny?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the inevitability of the Imamate passing to the Prophet’s progeny despite the historical rivalry between the Hashimite branches of Abbas and Ali. It underscores the Shia doctrine of *'Ilm Allah* (Divine Knowledge), affirming that the succession was pre-ordained and not contingent on human choice or marital avoidance. The narration serves as a key sign preceding the appearance of the Mahdi, linking the early prophetic era to the ultimate divine authority.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (2) Ali bin Ahmad al-Bandaneeji narrated from Obaydillah bin Musa al-Alawi from Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Khalid from Ibraheem bin Muhammad bin al-Mustaneer from Abdurrahman bin al-Qassim from his father that Abdullah bin Abbas had said:

“The Prophet (S) said to my father: “O Abbas, how much misfortunes my progeny will get from your progeny and then how much woes will come upon your progeny from my progeny!” Al-Abbas said: “Do I avoid sleeping with women?” The Prophet (S) said: “The will of Allah has already been determined and the decision is in His hand. But the end will be in the control of my progeny.”
